newsitem.title: USA: Stride Rite sales and income down.
newsitem.headline: Stride Rite sales and income down.

text.p: Footwear company Stride Rite Corp., maker of Keds sneakers and Sperry Top-Siders, Thursday reported declines in both sales and income for the third quarter.

The company's net income for the third quarter was down to $3.2 million from $3.5 million in the same period last year, a decline of 9 percent. Sales fell to $123.5 million, down 11 percent from $139.1 million in the third quarter of 1995.
Chairman and Chief Executive Robert Siegel said he does not expect a "quick turnaround" for Stride Rite, citing a backlog of orders for Keds and efforts to streamline the entire operation.
The company said it is investing in product development for the Keds line of sneakers in order to appeal to Keds' core customers, who are women between ages 25 and 44.

Sales in the division for the third quarter were down 23 percent from last year. Sales of Keds, the company's biggest product line, have been a continuing problem. Sales in 1995 fell 16 percent from 1994 and the division's president was replaced in January.
For the first nine months of the year, net income dropped 39 percent, from $12.5 million in 1995, to $7.6 million.
Sales dropped 12 percent in the period, to $366.6 million from last year's $418.3 million.
Under a three-year licensing deal with designer Tommy Hilfiger, Stride Rite will launch a new line of mens shoes in the spring of 1997.
Stride Rite stock was off 12.5 cents at $9.25 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange
